what: Two columns (block pillars) filling the screen are tied to the wheel and spin endlessly in opposite directions: wheel down moves the first column down and the second up, wheel up reverses. They chase the accumulated wheel distance with .15 lerp and push by the remaining distance each frame, so they keep gliding long after the wheel stops. The panel (or watch element) must be 98% in view to receive the wheel, and falls back to the start position once it drops below 10%. On the first column data-key="end" Give this to stand a block with its bottom edge on the tier floor

options.[data-fx-part=col]: Column (child) — two or more. A column’s children are blocks (heights may differ per block)
options.mult: Wheel multiplier, default window .08 · elsewhere .03 (original virtual-scroll mouseMultiplier)
options.watch: Element (css) that measures when to start receiving the wheel — defaults to the panel itself. The original is the blank space at the end of page scroll (.tiles__placeholder--last)
options.exit: When the wheel-up distance accumulates to this much, fires fx:twin-exit and releases the wheel (px or rem, default 0 = not released) — returns to page scroll after the original 140rem
options.fx:twin-live: Notifies detail.live when wheel capture starts and stops

note: Does not block wheel or touch (virtual-scroll preventTouch off) — used together with page scroll the page would scroll along, so as in the original, the panel fills the screen only when page scroll is at the end (or paused). At 1024 and below the original uses a one-line list instead of two columns

from.where: index.html .lj-tiles (two columns of product, photo and video tiles at the end of the first page — original tile_column: virtual-scroll mouseMultiplier .03 (Windows .08) · touchMultiplier .5, scrollY += (block moves by the remaining distance after (target − scrollY) × .15, left column layout left aligned to bottom, when 140rem stacks up Lenis returns to the 45% position)
